reconcile.connective: The PD commentators harmonize by time-frame: the wicked do prosper now, but God reserves their reckoning for the end, so both observations stand.

discrepancy.connective: Bart Ehrman presses the objection that Scripture's wisdom writers (Job, Ecclesiastes) simply observe that the wicked prosper, flatly against the texts asserting that evil destroys them — answers he reads as genuinely contradictory, not staged.

skeptic.name: Bart D. Ehrman
skeptic.work: God's Problem: How the Bible Fails to Answer Our Most Important Question—Why We Suffer

excerpts.excerpt_text: This principle Job here opposes, and maintains that God, in disposing men's outward affairs, acts as a sovereign, reserving the exact distribution of rewards and punishments for the future state.
excerpts.on_tension_rationale: Directly resolves the tension: concedes the wicked prosper now (Job 12:6) but assigns the just outcome (Ps 34:21) to a 'future state' — the eschatological harmonization.

excerpts.excerpt_text: The godly might suffer, but the Lord will reward them in the end. Similarly, the wicked might prosper for a time, but ultimately they will perish (1:6; 34:15-16).
excerpts.on_tension_rationale: Names both poles explicitly ('prosper for a time' vs Ps 34:21 'evil shall slay the wicked') and reconciles them by 'in the end'/'ultimately'.

excerpts.excerpt_text: to whom God for a while giveth prosperity, that afterward they should the more feel his heavy judgment when they lack their riches which were a sign of his mercy.
excerpts.on_tension_rationale: Same time-frame harmonization applied to Jeremiah 12:1: prosperity is granted 'for a while' precisely so 'heavy judgment' follows, reconciling the prospering-wicked with their destruction.

pd_work.resource: John W. Haley, An Examination of the Alleged Discrepancies of the Bible (Andover: W. F. Draper, 1874)
pd_work.author: John W. Haley
pd_work.note: Haley's harmonizing handbook treats the prosperity of the wicked versus the affliction of the righteous within the standard 'present prosperity, final judgment' framework that the PD commentators apply here.
